question: Vedantam Prahlad Sharma, born in Andhra Pradesh in 1923, was initiated into which of the following Indian classical dance styles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is one of the major classical dance forms of India, originating in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form derives its name from the village of **Kuchelapuram** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its **graceful movements, expressive gestures (Mudras),** and intricate footwork.
 
• Kuchipudi is a blend of **acting and dance**, often accompanied by Carnatic music, showcasing stories from Indian mythology and epics.
 
• Vedantam Prahlad Sharma, a renowned exponent of Kuchipudi, was instrumental in popularizing this art form across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms, originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, fixed upper torso movements, and expressive gestures (Mudras).
 
• Traditionally performed in temples as an offering to deities, it is closely associated with religious themes and devotion.
 
• Bharatanatyam is accompanied by Carnatic music and depicts stories from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form that originated in Northern India.
 
• It is characterized by rhythmic footwork, spins, and storytelling through facial expressions and hand gestures.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," meaning story, as the dance involves narrative performances.
 
• Kathak dancers often perform to Hindustani classical music, incorporating both devotional and secular themes.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form that originated in Odisha and is considered one of the oldest surviving dance traditions in India.
 
• It is known for its fluid movements, graceful postures, and tribhangi (three-bend) poses.
 
• Odissi performances are based on themes from Hindu mythology, particularly the works of Jayadeva and the stories of Lord Jagannath.
 
• The dance is performed with intricate hand gestures, facial expressions, and music that includes Odissi classical compositions.
